tool.name: acceptance-criteria-coverage
tool.toolSource: JEV repo, worktree review-5-plans-idea-folder-ce4d36 (read-only), round-2 tool copy plus round-3 diff in diff/tool-change-r3.diff

headline: Round 3 (4 stories of 9-10 criteria, 81-89 tests in 15-18 files, 2 repetitions): plain Claude 72/76 verdicts right, 4 of 8 runs fully right; Claude + shortlist 74/76, 6 of 8; tokens A 754,955 -> B 786,678 (+4.2%, within run-to-run noise); no run marked Covered falsely in either arm. The shortlist missed a decisive test in its top 3 for 11 of 38 criteria, so the tool is not yet shown to help. Top suggestion: measure recall at k=5 and 8 offline first and cut the Jev call if it adds no skippable saving.

tokens.source: subagent_tokens as reported by the Agent tool per case agent (not subagent_usage.mjs, which was not run)

evaluation.offlineRecall: 24 of 37 criteria with decisive gold had all decisive tests in the top-3 shortlist; 11 had none, 2 had some
deviations: Measurement-design fixes to the six criteria flagged by the round-2 Opus fixture review (resolved by the author, not by Opus): acc-11 AC-10 gold Missing -> Partial (test_reminder_goes_to_customer_email asserts the email, not the weekly cap); acc-12 AC-08 dropped (snapshot test always skips, no snapshot store); acc-13 AC-05 accepted set {Covered, Partial} (control total only implied); acc-13 AC-09 gold Missing -> Partial (cancel tests place and cancel an order but never assert the release); acc-14 AC-06 decisive set gains test_send_due_sends_at_run_time; acc-14 AC-09 dropped (same snapshot-only problem). Criteria: 38 in 4 stories (was 40); criterion ids are kept, so gaps appear (acc-12 has no AC-08, acc-14 no AC-09). See diff/fixture-key-fixes.diff.

Tool change: candidates --top default 5 -> 3 (discover.rank, discover.build_pack, CLI); unit test renamed to test_candidates_top_default_is_3; SKILL.md step 4. Digest already hid skippable pairs in round 2 (not changed). 19 unit tests pass (unit-tests output in recall/unit-tests-output.txt).

Arm A contamination: two arm-A runs read the neutral helper tool.mjs (acc-11 r2 and acc-13 r1, the latter also ran cat tool.mjs). Both were discarded, kept in answers/contaminated/ and in contaminated/ (work folders), and re-run as A2 in new work folders with tool.mjs removed from the folder. So in the A2 folders arm A has no helper file at all, unlike the other arm-A folders, which keep a helper that prints 'tool disabled'. Results count the A2 runs.

Forbid check: done by grepping tool_use inputs in each subagent transcript for tool.mjs, jev_skills, ac_coverage, build/r3 and /keys/ (after A2 re-run: 0 for both A2 runs and for all other A runs). subagent_usage.mjs --forbid was not run.
Answers were taken verbatim from the SubagentHandback message of each case agent (saved in answers/), not from the transcript's final text.
Token figures are the subagent_tokens reported per Agent call; subagent_usage.mjs was not run, so they are not the same counting method as earlier rounds.
Keys were kept out of the work folders (fixtures/ has no key; the keys are in evidence/ for grading only). Keys were written after the runs, as in round 1.
build_tool_report.mjs was not run for this folder; no report.html is produced in this round.
The SKILL.md change shows a whole-file diff in tool-change-r3.diff (line endings in the scratch copy); the real change is one line.
Round-3 recommendation was not sent to Opus: the result is not bad by the step-7b rule (B passes more full runs at +4.2% tokens).
